leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open and none is created by the recommended move as sequenced. The balance is positive now, and it only goes negative in the window between winning the auction and instant-selling Treu, which should be the same session. The bid is capped precisely so that the unwind is guaranteed: the ceiling is cash plus Treu at market value, so even at the maximum the balance returns positive on a single sale. Because Sirch is no longer being sold as a second leg, the squad never drops below eleven at any point in the sequence, and there is no path here that ends in a minus-one-hundred penalty. The one discipline that matters: never pre-sell. Selling before the auction resolves is how a lost auction turns into a ten-man squad.

binding_gap: There is no formation hole to fix — the eleven fill a legal shape today. What binds is the attack. Two forwards carry the line and the weakest fielded body is a full-back whose points-per-million is the worst in the squad. Hlozek replaces exactly that body, which is why this is an upgrade to a slot already covered rather than a repair, and why it is still the right move: the points gap between the incoming attacker and the outgoing defender is the largest available anywhere on the board. Nothing else comes close — the cleanest defender listed would improve on the same body by a rounding error and cannot be funded without losing points elsewhere, and the best midfield option on the board barely beats the man he would displace.
